characters.name: Robin Hood
characters.description: The Heroof the piece, this Robin is a younger, cheekier, and more easy-going variation of the traditional character. The Earl of Huntington and Lord of Locksley, Robin returns from five years fighting with King Richard in the Holy Land, to find that his lands and estates are now under the control of Guy of Gisborne. After refusing to conform to the corrupt laws that are now in place, Robin escapes into Sherwood Forest and begins a campaign of guerrilla warfare against the Sheriff, complete with the familiar "rob from the rich to give to the poor" system of wealth distribution. 10-Minute Retirement: InThe Return of the Kingand again inTotal Eclipse. All-Loving Hero: Despite his flaws, he genuinely loves the outlaws and the people he's promised to protect. Arranged Marriage:Downplayedbut it's established that Robin and Marian were betrothed from a very early age, suggesting this trope. BecomesPerfectly Arranged Marriagewhen they meet again and realize they do love each other mutually.

characters.name: Little John
characters.description: Little John is a bear and is Robin's loyal sidekick. Acrofatic: For a fat bear, he's just as agile and fast as Robin Hood. Attractive Bent-Gender: Little John gets wolf-whistled when in disguise. Baritone of Strength: With the deep, warm voice of Phil Harris used for the tough, boisterous bear, this is a given. Bears Are Bad News: To his opponents, at least — he's strong enough to fight multiplerhinosat once with a staff, and to hand theSheriffhis ass in a straight fight. He also holds a knife to theBig Bad's back and threatens to shank him in cold blood. But to everyone else, he's...

characters.name: Alan-a-Dale
characters.description: Alan-a-Dale is based off the minstrel of the same name from various Robin Hood legends, and is depicted as a rooster. Alan-a-Dale only states his name at the beginning of the film, where he also introduces himself as a minstrel. He functions as the film's narrator, using songs to tell the story. All-Knowing Singing Narrator: He is the one telling this story, but he also takes part in it. For instance, he helps Friar Tuck to chase down Sir Hiss at the archery tournament, and when he's arrested and thrown in jail, he already knows what's happening outside. The Bard: He sings songs, records lore, and carries a stringed instrument. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: Like Lady Kluck, he never wears shoes. Baritone of Strength:Inverted; while Alan's speaking voice and singing range are squarely baritone, he's decidedly aNon-Action Guy.

characters.name: Maid Marian
characters.description: Maid Marian is a vixen and is based on the character from the actual Robin Hood legend. Alliterative Name:MaidMarian. Babies Ever After:Discussedwhen Robin proposes to Marian.Robin:We'll have six children.Marian:Six? Oh, a dozen at least.And after they get married, Skippy tags along, saying, "Robin Hood's going to have kids. Sosomebodyhas to keep their eye on things." Discussedwhen Robin proposes to Marian.Robin:We'll have six children.Marian:Six? Oh, a dozen at least. And after they get married, Skippy tags along, saying, "Robin Hood's going to have kids. Sosomebodyhas to keep their eye on things."

characters.name: Lady Kluck
characters.description: Lady Kluck is a chicken and Maid Marian's lady-in-waiting. Acrofatic: Despite being "the fat one" (as Prince John calls her), she's quite athletic and anAction Girlthrough and through. Action Girl: Lady Kluck joins the brawl that caps the archery tournament. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: She isn't seen with any footwear. Beware the Silly Ones: She's a quite comical character, but also capable and strong. She was able to defeatall the guards, and strong enough tojudo-throw the Sheriff.

characters.name: Friar Tuck
characters.description: Friar Tuck is a badger and a kind-hearted priest who is good friends with Robin Hood and Little John. Badass Preacher: He delivers a righteous beating to the Sheriff for stealing from the poor box. Beware the Nice Ones: Do not take money from the poor box in front of Friar Tuck if you don't want a righteous beating. Big Eater: Downplayed compared to other versions of the character, but when he samples Robin Hood's burned stew, he cheerfully goes on eating it even after it makes him cough smoke rings. Even the Loving Hero Has Hated Ones: Friar Tuck is conveyed as a charitableBig Fun, though he spearheads the mocking campaign against Prince John and shows an indignant disdain for the Sheriff of Nottingham's bullying and tax gouging. When the latter finally hits hisRage Breaking Pointof taking money from the church's poor box, Tuck forcibly throws him out of the church to inflict anUnstoppable Ragebeatdown. Unfortunately for him, this trope was Exploited, as the Sheriff hadintentionally wound down his patienceand had his mooks ready outside to help overpower and arrest him for the assault, as one final lesson to the populace for underestimating Prince John's wrath.

characters.name: King Richard
characters.description: King Richard is the older brother of Prince John and the true king of England. Big Good: He could be considered this, beingThe Good Kingand beloved by all the good characters, even if his role in the plot is minor. Cain and Abel: The Abel to John's Cain for being a more benevolent royal. Foil: In contrast to his maneless and scrawny brother, King Richard has mane and is very muscular, representing him as the more mature and noble king than Prince John wishes to be. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: The Responsible to John's Foolish. While John is an arrogant, impatient, and pettyManchildwho wants to fuel his power through stealing from the poor, Richard is a kind, mature and sensible leader who rules the country professionally and doesn't look down on anyone below his status.

characters.name: Skippy Rabbit
characters.description: Skippy is an energetic 7-year-old rabbit. He lives with his mother and his siblings. He is the oldest boy in the family. Ascended Fanboy: He evolves from being Robin Hood's biggest fan to interacting with his hero. Robin even gives him his hat after the Sheriff takes his birthday gift. Badass Adorable: He's a cute rabbit with an adorable admiration of Robin Hood, and he fires an arrow at Prince John's butt. Barefoot Poverty: Implied to be the case, since most aristocracy is seen with footwear. It's a trait he shares with the rest of his family. Overlaps withBarefoot Cartoon Animal. Blue Is Heroic: Skippy wears a blue tunic and is one of the good guys.

characters.name: Mother Rabbit
characters.description: The kindly mother of Skippy and his many siblings. Bespectacled Cutie: She wears glasses (which hadn't been invented yet), and her gentle personality accentuates the sense of cuteness associated with them. Explosive Breeder: As per therabbit stereotype, she has about a dozen kids, only three of whom get any characterization (and onlyoneof whom gets a name). Good Parents: She's kind and loving toward her children. Mama Bear: When the Sheriff steals the farthing she'd planned to give Skippy for his birthday, sheuncharacteristicallyexplodes at him:Mother Rabbit:Have you no heart? We all scrimped and saved to give it to him.

characters.name: Prince John
characters.description: Prince John is a lion and the main villain of the story. 0% Approval Rating: His"The Villain Sucks" Songwas so successful that everyone, even Prince John's allies (Sir Hiss and the Sheriff), start singing it, much to Prince John's fury. Added Alliterative Appeal: Has a talent for alliterative nicknames, especially when addressing Sir Hiss (silly serpent, reluctant reptile, aggravating asp, etc.). He also calls Friar Tuck the "fat friar" and "corpulent cleric." Ambiguously Gay: Has a very campy inflection to his voice, behaves verychildishlyandeffeminatelyand is very quick to cry. As if all said wasn't obvious, he also lacks a mane (which, in lions, usually means low levels of testosterone). He's also very receptive to "Sir Reginald"'s compliments. He's also aMomma's Boy, something ofa now-forgotten stereotype of gay men. Kinda funny, since historically speaking,Richardis the one whose sexuality is up for debate, while the real John Lackland was a known womanizer with several legitimate and illegitimate children. Arch-Enemy: To Robin Hood of course, being that John is the one taxing the poor to the point of starvation and Robin is the one stealing the money back. John is also the one preventing Robin from marrying Maid Marian.

characters.name: Sir Hiss
characters.description: Sir Hiss is a snake and Prince John's loyal adviser. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Wears nothing but a feathered hat and a collar, and spectacles in one scene. Justified because he is a snake. Averted with his jail robes, which cover most of his coils. Aurora and Ariel can't help but gush over how adorable he looks in it inVillains Unite.Aurora: He's got a cape. I didn't notice the cape.Ariel: And he's got a little hat too.Aurora: Aw, he's just the cutest. Affably Evil: At least, he's certainly more pleasant than Prince John and the Sheriff. Alcohol Hic: When he's let out of the ale barrel, he is clearly drunk and his slurred hissing is just one indication. Beleaguered Assistant: The advisor to John and smarter than his foolish boss. What keeps him from being aDragon-in-Chiefis that he is much less ambitious, egotistical, or cruel than John. He'd qualify forCo Dragonwith the Sheriff, except that Hiss clearly doesn't take nearly as much joy in tormenting the populace as the Sheriff does.

characters.name: The Sheriff of Nottingham
characters.description: The gleefully sadistic Sheriff, who despite having ambitions to take over England, often seems to act the way he doesjust for the fun of it. Ambition Is Evil: Most of his crimes are born out of a desire to accumulate more power and wealth. And Starring: An unusual example, as Keith Allen is credited 'and Keith Allen' despite coming fourth out of nine names in the opening credits. Arch-Enemy: Robin is pitted against the Sheriff and Gisborne in equal measure, but in different regards with the Sheriff : with him it's very much a matter of moral and political differences as he is the tyrant of Nottingham. Back for the Finale: In Series 3, when he turns out to beNot Quite Dead.

characters.name: Nutsy and Trigger
characters.description: Trigger and Nutsy are the dimwitted vultures and the palace guards. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: They both only wear cloaks, and Trigger wears an iron helmet. Affably Evil: Nutsy is usually pretty cordial to whomever he's addressing. Bumbling Henchmen Duo: Two dim-witted and incompetent henchmen to Prince John and the Sheriff. Cassandra Truth: Trigger, on two occasions: the first is when he correctly suspects Robin (disguised as a beggar) to be a spy, and the second is when he rightfully worries that there may be a jailbreak in the works.

characters.name: Captain of the Guard/Captain Crocodile
characters.description: A crocodile who serves as, well, the Captain of Prince John's guards. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Wears a cape and a hat and nothing else. Badass Cape: His red cape denotes his status as Captain of the Guard. The Brute: Acts as backup muscle for the Sheriff. During hisSword Fightwith Robin, he actually holds his own, establishing himself as the most physically capable of the villains. It takes getting run over by the rhinos to put him out of action. Catchphrase: "Attention, everyone!" He first says it when starting the Tournament of the Golden Arrow, and says it again when announcing the finalists. The third time he says it,he's trampled by the rhino guardsbefore he can say anything else.

characters.name: Royal Guard
characters.description: Angry, Angry Hippos: Downplayed with the drummers who are hippos. Like the elephants, they serve as passive non-combatants, except for one brief instance when three of them aggressively chase after Lady Chuck at the archery tournament. Cruel Elephant: The trumpeteers and carriage drivers are Asian elephants. Although their behaviour isn't particularly cruel. Dumb Muscle: Despite being reasonably strong and very well-armed and armored, the rhinos in the guard aren't the sharpest tools in the shed. Aside from failing on multiple counts to capture Robin and his allies, they also charge at Prince John even though he begs them to stop. Fat Bastard: The rhinos are quite pot-bellied and they're are the brutish guards of the cruel and tyrannical Prince John. Imperial Stormtrooper Marksmanship Academy:Downplayed. While none of the arrows the wolves shoot wound Robin and his friends, one of them manages to hit Robin's bycocket.Robin: Hello! This one almost had my name on it, didn't it? They're getting better, you know. You've got to admit it! Theyaregetting better.

characters.name: As a whole
characters.description: Age Lift: In the original myth, the band of Merry Men were all adults. Here, they are pre-teens. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: Between the girls, Marian is the blonde, Winnifred is the redhead, and Barbara is the brunette. Blue Blood:Robin Hood, Wilfred, Winnifred and Barbara are descended from the Huntingtons, an old English noble family.Marian Lancaster also comes from a powerful English family, who also have a claim to the golden cross. Robin Hood, Wilfred, Winnifred and Barbara are descended from the Huntingtons, an old English noble family. Marian Lancaster also comes from a powerful English family, who also have a claim to the golden cross.

characters.name: Marian Lancaster
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Lady Marian in this incarnation is more cynical and serious-minded, and she makes up her mind to kill theRich Bastardwho's been plaguing her with her own hands.As a child. Adaptational Personality Change: She is aloof and sad on the inside because of her troubled past, less likely to open up to her friends, more serious-minded and tends to push herself past her limits on the battlefield. Action Girl: She learns to fight on her own and wield a sword under Little John's tutelageas well as harness the powers granted by the golden cross, eventually getting to the point where she leads raids against the nobles herself. Break the Cutie: Her misery is most apparent when she's forced to live with Alwine and Herefort and become the former'sMeal Ticketand the latter'sSex Slave(don't worry, he doesn't get to violate her, though he acts like a creep to her frequently). Alwine even beats her a couple of times to make her complacent. On the day of the wedding, Marian turns the tables by attempting to kill them, and escaping before either get a chance to carry out their plans with her. Driven to Suicide: On the day of her and Hereford's wedding, she makes her hatred known to him by attempting to slay him with a dagger, and then attempting to take her own life as aLast Stand.

characters.name: Winnifred Huntington
characters.description: Anger Born of Worry: She slaps Barbara for wandering into a dangerous situation for a wolf pup's sake, to the shock of everyone else. She instantly regrets this and begins crying, admitting to Barbara she missed her. Damsel in Distress: Winnifred is kidnapped by Alwine's forces once they see her with Marian's cross (which was actually given to her by John) and mistake her for the Lady herself. She's then used as bait for Robin Hood once Alwine pieces together that she's her cousin. She'sthenkidnapped by bounty hunters who want to hurt Duncan and use her as a hostage. Dub Name Change: From Winnifred toDialain the Arabic dub. Hidden Depths: Despite being raised rich, she has some knowledge of medical care, as she tends to John and Tuck when they're sick. Oblivious to Love: John has eyes for Winnifred, but she never realizes themuntil the finale. John does hint it here and there, but she assumes he cares for her out of a sense of duty like he does for the other bandits.

characters.name: Wilfred Huntington
characters.description: In-Series Nickname: His name is Wilfred, but everyone calls him Will for short. Non-Action Guy: Unlike his cousin, Will isn't much of a fighter, but his skills lie in espionage. He escorts Marian out of the castle while the others are distracted, and regularly steals from the nobles without getting caught. Red Baron: Attempted. He dubs himself "Will of the Gale" after being trained in stick combat by Mutch but it doesn't catch on.

characters.name: Barbara Huntington
characters.description: Blush Sticker: To emphasize that she's the youngest of the bandits, she has prominent pink blush stickers on her cheeks. Dub Name Change:From Barbara toJennyin the English, Greek and Colombian Spanish dubs.From Barbara toJuliein the Arabic dub. From Barbara toJennyin the English, Greek and Colombian Spanish dubs. From Barbara toJuliein the Arabic dub. Friend to All Living Things: Like Robin Hood, she has an affinity for animals. She tames a dangerous lion with kindness, and when she finds a stray wolf puppy, she actually tries to take the little thing in. She ends up releasing it into the wild because it's his natural habitat, but the puppy grows quite fond of her.

characters.name: Mutch
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Amongst the bandits. He lets John walk all over him and boss him around, is often humiliated because of his own obliviousness, and is treated like a complete joke by everyone despite being the chief's second-in-command. He even runs away crying in the second episode because everyone's so mean to him, though he returns because he has nowhere else to go. Really Royalty Reveal:Mutch is eventually revealed to be a descendant of the King of England, meaning that he has a claim to the throne. Screw This, I'm Outta Here:During his coronation, he decides it isn't worth being a puppet of Alwin's and announces his defection to the entire public.

characters.name: Lord Alwine
characters.description: Aristocrats Are Evil: Lord Alwine is part of the nobility, and initially places heavy taxes on the citizenry before going further and appropriating their properties, and he doesn't care if some of his actions (like opening a mine near the forest, leading it to getting infected from the waste) affect the lives of others. He also tries to adopt Marian with the intention of exploiting her. Corrupted Character Copy: He's based on the Sheriff of Nottingham from the original myths, except while the Sheriff was justified to a degree (if you go by the interpretation that he was just doing his jobs topping Robin from burgling innocents), Alwine is a tyrant who squashes anyone who dares stand up to him and thinks nothing of slaughtering children. Dastardly Whiplash: He's got the look and attitude down pat. Curling black mustache, lanky build, exaggerated crooked nose, and a cartoonish tendency to revel at his own wickedness. Though the story plays with the idea that he might be redeemable, he ultimately blows off his chance and proves to be a straight up bastard 'till the bitter end. Establishing Character Moment: In the first episode, he's seen sitting on his horse, while leading the scourge on Huntington castle.Destroy the castle! Burn it to the ground! Let this be a lesson to all those who disobey me. Greed: He has an endless lust for other people's wealth and political power, so much that he even tries totrick Robin Hood into aiding him usurp the King and rule England.

characters.name: Bishop of Hereford
characters.description: Dirty Old Man: HisEstablishing Character Momentis him fooling around with scantily clad women at one of the noble's parties. And as his attraction to Marian shows, he does NOT consider age to be a barrier when it comes to potential prospects. Establishing Character Moment: He is introduced drinking and feeling up women, showcasing his hedonistic and un-serious nature in contrast to Alwine's grim villainy. Fish Eyes: His right eye is static and doesn't move. Inconsistent Spelling: Is itHerefordorHartford? Old Man Marrying a Child: Baron Alwine threatened to end the Lancaster line unless they promised him Marian and the cross. While he didn't have any interest in Marian beyond using her as a puppet leader, Bishop Hereford was head over heels for her and wanted to make her his wife. Alwine had no problem with it. Subverted, as on the day of the wedding Marian tries to kill him, before declaring their potential marriage dead and running away to become a rebel.

characters.name: Sir Gilbert Whitehand
characters.description: The Ace: Out of all of Lord Alwine's Knights, Gilbert is the strongest, most diligent, well-feared, and skilled enough to fight even when caught off-guard. Age-Gap Romance: He loves Marian, who seems to be a decade apart from him. He isn't bothered by the fact that he is an adult while she is a child. All Love Is Unrequited: He loves Marian, but Marian never viewed him the same way, even though he was someone very dear to her heart. Always Save the Girl: His first priority is Marian and her safety, and he will do anything to keep her safe and make her happy.Even if it means going to jail for disobeying Lord Alwine. Amnesiac Hero:He survives falling into the ravine, at the cost of losing his memory. Though he doesn't recall his own name, he is able to piece tigether that he is a Knight, and continues to fight as one in the dark.

characters.name: Cleo Whitehand
characters.description: Boyish Short Hair: She has short black hair styled in a bob cut. You Killed My Father: After Gilbert dies, she becomes swarmed with grief because he's the only family she's had since their parents died, and swears to get revenge on Robin Hood.

characters.name: All Outlaws
characters.description: Adaptation Personality Change: Interestingly, three of the main Merry Men seem to swap personalities from how they were in the ballads.Will Scarlett in the ballads was a charismatic and somewhat morally greyPretty Boy, who's backstory had him as a rougher character until he joined Robin Hood. In the show, this better describes Allan-a-Dale.Allan-a-Dale in the ballads was a foppishPlucky Comic Reliefcharacter who enjoyed singing (being a bard), hadUndying Loyaltyto Robin, but was the least action-inclined. In the show, this better describes Much.Much in the ballads was defined by his full title: Much the Miller's Son; he was a young teenager, son of a local peasent worker, was more reserved, but was very good in a fight. In the show, this better describes Will Scarlett. Will Scarlett in the ballads was a charismatic and somewhat morally greyPretty Boy, who's backstory had him as a rougher character until he joined Robin Hood. In the show, this better describes Allan-a-Dale. Allan-a-Dale in the ballads was a foppishPlucky Comic Reliefcharacter who enjoyed singing (being a bard), hadUndying Loyaltyto Robin, but was the least action-inclined. In the show, this better describes Much. Much in the ballads was defined by his full title: Much the Miller's Son; he was a young teenager, son of a local peasent worker, was more reserved, but was very good in a fight. In the show, this better describes Will Scarlett. Badass Crew: The outlaws are a tight and effective combative team (at least in the first two series) that can operate as anything from guerilla fighters to elaborate con-artists.

characters.name: Much
characters.description: Robin’s faithful manservant who accompanies him to the Holy Land and who is promised an Earldom by Robin on their return to England. Disappointed at the loss of Bonchurch Estate and all the comforts that it entails, but too devoted to Robin to do anything but follow him into Sherwood, Much is simultaneously the most loyal and most reluctant member of the gang. Big Eater: That is, he is when the circumstances allow (which isn't very often while living rough in the forest). He is often talking about food though. Bumbling Sidekick: Though he was actually quite an accomplished warrior, he's oftentreatedlike this due to his worrisome nature andMotor Mouthtendencies. Butt-Monkey: To the extent that the fanbase started a "Treat Much Right" campaign. The Caretaker: He considers Robin's wellbeing and general health his responsibility, and his life essentially revolves around his master.

characters.name: Allan-a-Dale
characters.description: A opportunistic thief, con-artist, pick-pocket and compulsive liar, this Allan strays far from his traditional role as a minstrel (ironically, he is actually left out when the other outlaws dress up as minstrels). The only outlaw that has no personal investment in the cause that Robin Hood is fighting (and often pointing out that as a poor person himself, he should have a share of any stolen goods) Allan sticks around just for the fun of it – or perhaps for want of anything better to do. In early Series 2 he is approached by Guy of Gisborne andcoerced into becoming a spy. After a short stint asThe Mole, he is found out and openly joins Guy as his right-hand man. Always Second Best: Allan seems himself as this, and makes it part of hisFreudian Excuse. Anti-Hero: Allan doesn't particularly share or believe in Robin's ideals, and is only with the outlaws via circumstances forcing it, as best shown by his argument with Much in "Sisterhood". Being Tortured Makes You Evil: At least, this is Allan's excuse when Robin finds out he's been working for Gisborne.

characters.name: Will Scarlett
characters.description: An apprentice carpenter in Locksley, Will’s mother died of starvation in the attempt to keep Will and his little brother alive, and his father lost his hand after taking the punishment for his children when they steal food to eat. The youngest member of the gang at eighteen, Will joins the gang after Robin saves him from hanging and due to his deep hatred of the Sheriff, something that can often cause his low-simmering temper to rise up. The most sensible, moral and sensitive member of the gang, Will falls in love with Djaq and decides to stay with her in the Holy Land at the conclusion of Series 2. Accidental Pervert: He approaches a topless Djaq whilst she's cleaning herself for prayer.He doesn't realize she's a womanuntil his eyes suddenly drop to chest-level. The Baby of the Bunch: He is the youngest outlaw at eighteen, and is often treated as a little brother by the rest of the gang. Battle Couple: In Series 2 he and Djaq are often paired up on missions and in combat situations.

characters.name: Djaq
characters.description: Following in the newer tradition of having a Saracen character join Robin Hood’s gang, Djaq is the first female to hold the honour, making her aTwofer Token Minority. Contributing her skills as a physician, scientist, linguist and swordswoman to the team, she became quite popular, largely due to the genuine affection she had for her fellow outlaws, and her role asDeadpan Snarker. Action Girl: Has combat training thanks to her time disguised as a boy, fighting in the Third Crusade. Affirmative Action Girl: She's introduced halfway through the first season, joining Marian as one of only two main female characters. Angsty Surviving Twin:Downplayedsince therealDjaq is dead before the show begins, but "our" Djaq calls herself such in memory of her twin brother, and clearly carries a lot of grief for him. Badass Adorable: She's tiny, adorable, hasPuppy-Dog Eyes...and will rip your arms off if you get her angry.

characters.name: Royston White
characters.description: An original member of Little John's outlaws. Anyone Can Die:The first major character to get killed off, though perhaps mildlysubvertedconsidering he wasthe only character not to appearin any of the legends. Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: He chooses to betray the other outlaws when his mother is taken captive by the Sheriff. Forgotten Fallen Friend:After his death, no one ever mentions him again. However, Little John does keep his outlaw tag and later passes it onto his son, somewhat fitting considering he says that Roy "was like a son to me." Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He loves his mother, anddies for a baby.

characters.name: Brother Tuck
characters.description: A mysterious monk who arrives from travelling the world (having left the church after he became disillusioned) at the start of Series 3, and who joins the outlaws after inspiring Robin to recommit to the cause. Adaptational Attractiveness: Every single depiction of Tuck up until David Harewood portrayed him as a short, portly, aging man with a shaved tonsure. In comparison, this Tuck is tall, muscular, in his mid-forties, and missing the typical monkish haircut. Adaptational Badass: Friar Tuck isn't usually directly involved in the combat himself, but this version is very competent in battle. Adaptational Goal Change: Most versions of Tuck portray him as aGood Shepherdwho is motivated by his strong Christian faith and an understanding that Robin is helping the poor and downtrodden. This Tuck is more politically motivated, who wants to use Robin's pre-existing stature as a hero to galvanize the people of England into rising up against tyranny. Adaptational Late Appearance: In various retellings Friar Tuck is usually on-board with Robin's battle against the Sheriff right from the word go. In contrast, this show's take on Tuck doesn't turn up until the third series.

characters.name: Kate
characters.description: A village girl who joins the team. Always Save the Girl: The outlaws will usually drop whatever they're otherwise doing in order to rush off and save her. Ambiguously Absent Parent: Kate lives with her mother and younger siblings with no mention of a father. And Starring: The opening credits of Series 3 ended with "And Joanne Froggatt." Betty and Veronica: The Betty to Isabella's Veronica, right down to the hair colour.

characters.name: Lady Marian
characters.description: Dropping the usual “maid” part of her name in favour of "lady", this version of Marian operated as Robin’s eyes and ears within the castle, but also had an agenda of her own what with her secret identity as the Nightwatchman, a masked and hooded figure who distributed food parcels amongst the poor. The centre of a love triangle between Robin Hood and Guy of Gisborne, shedies at Gisborne’s handsat the end of Series 2. Action Girl: She's trained in combat and has aSecret Identityas the Nightwatchman, who distributes money and supplies to the poor. All Girls Like Ponies: After a squabble, Gisborne tries to placate her with a beautiful white pony — the gesture works. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Ultimatelysubverted. Though she's clearly attracted to Gisborne, she eventually reaches the end of her patience with his steadfast refusal to leave the Sheriff's service and stop working against the rightful king. Of course, after becoming an outlaw, Robin is something of a "bad boy" too...

characters.name: Guy of Gisborne
characters.description: The Sheriff of Nottingham’s right-hand man and competitor for Marian’s affections. Alliterative Name:GuyofGisborne. Ambition Is Evil: His entire arc is based on this. Antagonist in Mourning: Throughout Series 3, in which he grapples with his grief and guilt overmurdering Marian. Arch-Enemy: Gisborne, having taken Robin's lands and beingthe most consistant physical threat Robin and his men have to facewould be enough to make him qualify for this trope but the fact that he is vying for the love of Marian like Robin doesjust makes it all the more personal. Gisborne fits more firmly into the role because of the events of the following two episodes:InTattoo. What Tattoo?, it’s revealed that Gisborne wassent as an assassin to kill King Richards in the Holy LandsandRobin has to be physically restrained from killing a tied up Guy on the spotbecause of his adoration and loyalty for his king and because of the consequences had he succeeded.InWe Are Robin Hood !Gisborne's murder ofMariancauses Robin to (temporarily) lose hope in his campaign and drives him to try and kill Gisborne as revenge inTotal Eclipse.

characters.name: Isabella of Gisborne
characters.description: Appearing in the third season as Guy’snever before seen or mentioned little sister, Isabella entered the show on the run from her sadistic husband. An enigmatic presence throughout her eight episodes, she is the centre of the political machinations that drove the final season. Initially introduced as aReplacement Goldfishfor Robin and asThe Molewithin the castle, Isabellasubvertedexpectations by striking out on her own, flirting with Prince John, performing aFace–Heel Turnand winning herself the position of Sheriff of Nottingham. Alas, Poor Villain: She's so mentally unhinged by the final few episodes, it's difficult not to feel sorry for her. In one of her last scenes, she looks regretfully overthe dead body of her brotherand on realizing that the castle is about to explode, she looks strangely at peace with her impending death. Ambition Is Evil: Her need for power and security eventually overcomes her better instincts. Attempted Rape: What her husband Thornton is trying to do before she kills him. Ax-Crazy: She becomes this after Robin dumps her.

characters.name: Sir Edward of Knighton
characters.description: Marian's father and the former Sheriff of Nottingham. I Will Only Slow You Down: He utters this trope by name after he's fatally stabbed. Recurring Character: Though not in the opening credits, he's in almost every episode up until his death. Senseless Sacrifice: Edward dies in order to deliver the Pact of Nottingham into Robin's hands, aMcGuffinthat the outlaws unfortunately forget to take to the Holy Land when they set off in pursuit of Marian. It would have providedKing Richardwith definitive proof that Prince John was plotting treason against him, and although Robin convinces him eventually, it's onlyafterRichard sets off a chain of events that results inMarian's death. The Pact is never mentioned in Series 3, but by that stage, it was worthless anyway.

characters.name: Archer
characters.description: Guy and Robin's half-brother. Would have (presumably) become the new Robin but for the show's cancellation. Distinguishing Mark: He has a birthmark shaped like an arrowhead, which provides the inspiration for his name, and an easy way to identify him. Doubles as aBirthmark of Destinygiven that he takes over the mantle of Robin Hood. Easily Forgiven: He sold Guy and Robin out to Isabella for money, and also soldVaizeyByzantine fire. He ends up a member of the gang with little comment to him being untrustworthy. Admittedly, like Guy, he was thrown into the situation with them and they didn't really have much of a choice in the matter. 11th-Hour Ranger: He is introduced as an adult in the third-to-last episode of the entire series, and joins the team only at the end of thesecond-to-last episode. Katanas Are Just Better: He even appears toDual Wieldthem somehow (despite them being two-handed weapons).

characters.name: Carter
characters.description: A Crusader who returned to England from the Holy Land seeking revenge against Robin for his brother's death. Hired as an assassin by the Sheriff, he successfully infiltrates the outlaw camp, but performs aHeel–Face Turnafter Robin tells him the truth about how his brother died. Appearing in only two episodes, this guest star became surprisingly popular among the fanbase. Back for the Finale: He reappears in the second season finale. Dropped a Bridge on Him: He's killed by the Sheriff in a scene that lasts no more than two seconds, a death that is then entirely overshadowed by Marian's (thoughaccording to the DVD commentary, the grave next to Marian's with the shield belongs to him, so it can be assumed that the outlaws gave himsomesort of funeral). Sudden Sequel Death Syndrome: Carter survives his first episode as a guest star, but is killed off in his next appearance. Redemption Equals Death: After trying to kill Robin and the other outlaws in his first appearance, he dies trying to assist them in his second.

characters.name: Luke Scarlett
characters.description: Will Scarlett's little brother. The Other Darrin: Was played by Jonathan Readwin inWill You Tolerate This?, and by Christian Cooke inThe Angel of Death.Lampshadedin his second appearance when he tells his brother that he's "not so little" anymore. Lampshadedin his second appearance when he tells his brother that he's "not so little" anymore.

characters.name: Rebecca
characters.description: Kate's mother, a potter in Locksley village. Bitch Slap: She gives one to Kate after hearing the news that her son Matthew has been killed. Entitled Bitch: Her worst moment is when she blames Robin for her son's death and angrily asks him where he was when he died. You can almostseeRobin thinking: "I was right next to him, watching as your stupid daughter kept messing up my plans to save him." Insane Troll Logic: She blames Robin for Matthew's death, even though Guy killed him, Kate endangered him, and Matthew himself had no sense of self-preservation at all. Jerkass Has a Point: To a certain extent, sheisright when she points out that fraternizing with outlaws will only bring trouble to her door. However, she refuses to admit that they save lives and help people far more than they endanger them.

characters.name: The Outlaws
characters.description: Act of True Love: Robin deciding to stick around in Nottingham (where he could easily be found by Godrey and his mooks) and robbing theCorrupt Churchof the grain to plant Nottingham's fields could easily be seen as this. Yes, he wanted Walter to tell him about his past and help the people of Nottingham, but the look on his face when he told Marion what he'd done and she thanked him said it all. He mostly did it for her. Adaptation Name Change: Loxley instead of Locksley. Been There, Shaped History: Various versions of the tale have given Robin Hood questionable degrees of historical importance, but few have gone so far as to credit him with delivering the first draft of theMagna Carta(written by his own father) to the barons who petitioned King John for its signature. Big "NO!": Utters one of these at the final battle whenMarion is taken down by Godfrey. Blood Oath: Alan points out to him when he swears to return Sir Robert's sword that this trope is in effect, since Robin had nicked his hand. Robin blows this off but still returns the sword to Sir Robert's father.

characters.name: The Royals
characters.description: Artistic License – History: The film says Richard has no children which is incorrect: he didn’t have any legitimate children. He had an acknowledged illegitimate son named Phillip and may have had others. He’s also shown speaking English and insulting the French. Since he was a second son, he wasn’t raised to be the heir to the English throne. He was raised to be the heir of his mother’s realm of Aquitaine, where he spent most of his life. He spent only six months of his reign in England and didn’t speak any English. His great-nephew Edward I is believed to have been the first post-Conquest king to speak English fluently and it would be another 200 years before Henry IV became the first native speaker. Bait the Dog: The setup for Richard asking Robin what he thinks of his crusade implies he'll reward him for his honesty. Instead he puts him in stocks with his gang. Boisterous Bruiser: He is boisterous and larger than life, growling dramatically like his namesake when he washes in the morning and rides in battle. Brutal Honesty: When King Richard asks for his opinion of the crusade, Robin answers honestly that it was a pointless waste of life. From the setup in the previous scene, it almost seems that King Richard was going to reward Robin for his honesty and set himself as aReasonable Authority Figure. Instead he puts Robin and his gang in the stocks for their trouble. Casual Danger Dialogue: When Robert Loxley is calling for a physician to tend to Richard's fatal neck wound, Richard asks, "why Robert, are you ill?"

characters.name: Nottingham
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: Sir Walter (along with Sir Godfrey) is anOriginal Characterwho doesn't appear in any of the Robin Hood legends. Dirty Old Man: This scene:Walter:I woke this morning with a tumescent glow. Eighty-four! A miracle.Marion:[as Robin smirks] I'd always wondered at the private conversations of men... Old Soldier: Sir Walter isn't afraid to swing a sword at his enemies, despite being 84 years old and nearly blind. Papa Wolf: Upon learning the man before him was his son's murderer, he flew into a rage against him, despite being very old and blind. He was even able to wound Godfrey before he was taken down. Sacrificial Lion: He is killed mercilessly by Godfrey.
